column1: # The hover box of the Cheats window: what a cheat (or a choice, by its title) does, in full. Read by tools/catalog.py.
# <name as the window shows it><TAB><text>. Say what the grey line under the cheat doesn't: no keys, no "who needs it".

column2: Switches on a debug function the developers left in the game. The original author of the code gives no detail about what it shows; back up your save first.
Dialogue and message boxes print their letters much faster, so you don't wait for each line to finish. Nothing else changes.
The quick save can be used again and again: it is not used up and does not have to be loaded and deleted first.

Gives the party the wings back in the opening of the game (Angel Falls). Press L+R+START+Up, walk into or out of a house, then press L+R+START+Down and enter or leave a house again. Needs three or fewer characters in the party.
Keeps the gold in the bank at the maximum (9,999,999) the whole time. Spending from it refills it.
Keeps the gold you carry at the maximum (9,999,999) the whole time. Whatever you spend comes back at once.
Sets the mini medals you carry to 999 and keeps them there, enough for every prize.
Your own inn (the Quester's Rest) jumps to its highest level with every upgrade built. It does not add guests by itself.
Repairs the guest book when it hangs the game because of a damaged entry. Use it once, then look at the guest book again.
You walk through walls and obstacles on the field while it is on. You can leave the map: save first, and switch it off before you go through a door.

column1: Every vocation can use all equipment
column2: Removes the vocation check from equipment: any character can equip any weapon, shield and armour, whatever their vocation.

column1: Highlight an item in the bag
column2: In the item bag, move the cursor to an item and press START+R: you get 99 of it. Only works for items already in the bag (not in the Stornway inn).
Raises the hero's attack, defence and agility to the maximum. It has to be switched on again after a level-up or a change of equipment, because the game recalculates those values.
All party tricks (the gestures you can assign to the party) are learned at once.
Every character's stats (HP, MP, attack, defence, agility, deftness...) are set to 999. They stay at 999 until the game recalculates them, for example after a level-up.
Opens every extra menu of the game's start menu: battle records, allocate skill points and the party tricks screen, even if the story hasn't unlocked them yet.

column1: Re-Zoom to any location, L+Start Copy, Zoom, L+A Paste
column2: Zoom is the spell that teleports you to a place you have already visited. With this cheat L+START stores the spot you are standing on, and after casting Zoom to somewhere else, L+A pastes the stored spot as your destination, so you can return to exactly that place. The spot is the one the game remembers after the screen blacks out (through a door, leaving the battle records).
Special guests (the story characters who can stay at the inn) no longer need their conditions to be met before they can check in.
Resets the special guests so that they can visit your inn again, as if they had never been.

column1: Hold [L/R] Walkthrough A Door/Stairs to Go Observatory/Stornway
column2: Hold L or R while you walk through a door or over stairs and you are sent to the Observatory or to Stornway instead of the normal place. The author's title does not say which button leads where; let go of L and R for normal doors.
Lets you throw away equipment that the game says cannot be discarded, such as key items worn by a character.
On the world map the camera can be turned all the way round with L and R, not only a little to each side.
In towns and dungeons the camera can be turned all the way round with L and R.
Makes the party members invisible on the field (you still move and fight normally). Pick whether only some or all of them vanish.

column1: Hold [A] Enemy Wil Never Chase After You
column2: Monsters stop chasing you while you hold A. Battle still starts if you walk into one.

column1: No Random Battles, Push Start+Right for Instant Battle
column2: Switches random battles off, so nothing attacks you on the ship. Press START+RIGHT to start a battle whenever you want one.
Press L+R and monsters near you are pushed away, so you can slip past them. According to the author it works on the world map and in caves.
While it is on, press START+UP in the game and the in-game clock jumps to daytime. Do it now does it at once.

column1: Night Time, push Start and Down
column2: While it is on, press START+DOWN in the game and the in-game clock jumps to night. Do it now does it at once.

Teaches every party member the Zoom spell, which teleports you to any place you have visited (you cast it outdoors, from the spell menu). Meant for a new game; it does not unlock new places by itself.
Adds every place in the game to the Zoom list, so you can teleport anywhere, also to places you have never visited. Needs Zoom to be known by someone (see Enable Zoom).

column1: All Visitors Rooms Unlocked for Inn
column2: Every guest room of your inn is unlocked, so guests can be placed in all of them.
Marks every vocation as unlocked in your save, so you can switch to any of them at the Vocation Guild. This version changes the save data (v1 only changes the menu).
Fills in the defeated-monster list for every monster, and, depending on the option, also marks their item drops as seen (127 drops each).
Lets you do alchemy (kracking) without having the ingredients; the recipe is cooked anyway.
The alchemy ingredients are not used up when you cook something, you keep all of them.

column1: Alchemy ingredients on the field never run out
column2: The sparkly spots on the field can be picked again and again, so the ingredients never run out.
Every alchemy attempt turns into an alchemiracle: you get a better result than the recipe promises.
Sets the hero's real hit points (the number the game uses in battle) to 9999 and keeps it there.
Sets the hero's current hit points to 9999, the number shown on screen right now. If the maximum is lower, the game may pull it back down.
Sets the hero's real magic points to 9999 and keeps them there.
Sets the hero's current magic points to 9999, the number shown on screen right now.
The hero's HP is refilled to the maximum every frame, so damage never sticks. In battle too.
The hero's MP is refilled to the maximum every frame, so casting costs nothing.
Player 2's HP is refilled to the maximum every frame.
Player 2's MP is refilled to the maximum every frame.
Player 3's HP is refilled to the maximum every frame.
Player 3's MP is refilled to the maximum every frame.
Player 4's HP is refilled to the maximum every frame.
Player 4's MP is refilled to the maximum every frame.
Puts 99 of every consumable item (herbs, seeds, potions...) into the bag. The author notes that it may not contain every item.
Puts 99 of every weapon into the bag. This replaces that part of the bag, so save first.
Puts 99 of every shield into the bag (replaces that part of the bag, save first).

column1: Bag: 99 of every upper body armour
column2: Puts 99 of every upper-body armour into the bag (replaces that part of the bag, save first).

column1: Bag: 99 of every lower body armour
column2: Puts 99 of every lower-body armour into the bag (replaces that part of the bag, save first).
Puts 99 of every helmet and hat into the bag (replaces that part of the bag, save first).
Puts 99 of every glove and gauntlet into the bag (replaces that part of the bag, save first).
Puts 99 of every pair of boots and shoes into the bag (replaces that part of the bag, save first).
Puts 99 of every accessory into the bag (replaces that part of the bag, save first).
Puts 99 of every consumable item into the bag, once, when you press the button. Replaces that part of the bag, so save first.

column1: Monsters always drop a treasure chest
column2: Every defeated monster leaves a treasure chest behind, not only the rare ones.

column1: Treasure Map Boss Always Drop Chest
column2: The boss of a treasure map (grotto) always leaves its chest.
The blue chests of a grotto close again. Open a chest, open the battle records or equipment screen (or re-enter the floor) and it is closed; use it to loot the same chest again.
Sets the wireless play time in your records to its maximum.
Sets the total play time in your records to its maximum.
Sets the number of battles won in your records to its maximum.
Sets the number of treasures found in your records to its maximum.
Sets the number of guests that visited your inn in your records to its maximum.
Sets the number of completed quests in your records to its maximum.
Sets the number of items you forged in your records to its maximum.

column1: Fill in All ? ? ? of Extra Quest
column2: Fills in the unknown (? ? ?) entries of the extra quests list, so the quests show their names. It does not complete the quests.
Every alchemy recipe appears in the Alchenomicon as known but not yet made.
Every alchemy recipe is marked as known and already made.
Gives you every accolade (title) at once.
Makes all extra quests available. Use it on a new game before accepting any quests and do not go online afterwards.
Makes all extra quests available (another method than V1). Use after you have finished quests 2, 117 and 120 and do not go online afterwards.

column1: 100% Monster List, Wardrobe, Item List and Alchenomicon
column2: Completes the monster list, the wardrobe, the item list and the Alchenomicon in one go.
Completes the monster list (every monster counted as met and defeated).
Your party acts before the monsters in the first round of every battle.

column1: Can Always Use Coup de Grace
column2: The coup de grace (the strong finishing attack) can be chosen at any time, not only when the game would offer it. The menu entry still looks grey.
A normal attack hits every enemy instead of one.
Activate it before you attack: the next hit kills the enemy outright.
The enemies in the battle fall asleep.
The enemies in the battle are poisoned.
The enemies in the battle are stunned and lose their turns.
The enemies in the battle are confused.
Every attack of your party is a critical hit.
Hold A and RIGHT just before a battle starts: you face three of the same monster instead of the usual mix.
Hold L in battle and the party is covered by Soul Asylum, so nothing can hurt it.
Press Y in battle: the first party member goes to high tension.
Press Y in battle: the second party member goes to high tension.
Press Y in battle: the third party member goes to high tension.
Press Y in battle: the fourth party member goes to high tension.

column1: Enable Coup de Grace - 1st Character (Press X)
column2: Press X in battle: the first party member may use the coup de grace.

column1: Enable Coup de Grace - 2nd Character (Press X)
column2: Press X in battle: the second party member may use the coup de grace.

column1: Enable Coup de Grace - 3rd Character (Press X)
column2: Press X in battle: the third party member may use the coup de grace.

column1: Enable Coup de Grace - 4th Character (Press X)
column2: Press X in battle: the fourth party member may use the coup de grace.

column1: To View Character Animation Before A Battle
column2: Switch it on right before a battle to see the characters' entrance animation in that one battle.
Helps with treasure maps: in treasure map mode, press R while you zoom (Zoom) and the cursor jumps to the exact spot of the grotto's entrance on the world map.
Battles give 2, 4, 8... up to 128 times the experience. Pick one option; it only changes what you are given after a battle.
Battles give 2, 4, 8... up to 128 times the gold. Pick one option.
Spending skill points does not use them up: you can put points into every skill and take them back at will.

column1: 1 Skill Point Added Equal To All Skills Max
column2: Adds one skill point to every skill of the character until each skill is at its maximum.
Gives the hero 500 skill points to spend.
Gives player 2 500 skill points to spend.
Gives player 3 500 skill points to spend.
Gives player 4 500 skill points to spend.

column1: All Member in Party Skill Points x500
column2: Gives every party member 500 skill points to spend.
Changes the hero's vocation to the one you pick.
Changes player 2's vocation to the one you pick.
Changes player 3's vocation to the one you pick.
Changes player 4's vocation to the one you pick.

column1: Max EXP in every vocation: Hero
column2: Fills the experience of every vocation of the hero to the maximum, so every vocation counts as mastered.

column1: Max EXP in every vocation: Player 2
column2: Fills the experience of every vocation of player 2 to the maximum.

column1: Max EXP in every vocation: Player 3
column2: Fills the experience of every vocation of player 3 to the maximum.

column1: Max EXP in every vocation: Player 4
column2: Fills the experience of every vocation of player 4 to the maximum.
Changes how fast you walk on the field: slower (x0.5) or faster (x1.5, x2...). Pick one option.
In battle, enemy number 1 has 1 HP left, so any hit defeats it.
In battle, enemy number 2 has 1 HP left.
In battle, enemy number 3 has 1 HP left.
In battle, enemy number 4 has 1 HP left.
In battle, enemy number 5 has 1 HP left.
In battle, enemy number 6 has 1 HP left.
In battle, enemy number 1 has no MP left, so it can't cast.
In battle, enemy number 2 has no MP left.
In battle, enemy number 3 has no MP left.
In battle, enemy number 4 has no MP left.
In battle, enemy number 5 has no MP left.
In battle, enemy number 6 has no MP left.
The hero's head is much bigger. Pick the size; Start+L/R can change it while you play.
Changes the hero's whole body size on the field; hold A and L or R to change it while you play.

Experience from a battle is handed out the other way round: the party member with the lowest level gets what the highest one would have got, and the other way round. Good for catching up a weak character.

column1: Metal slimes only, in the areas that have them
column2: In every area where metal monsters (metal slime, liquid metal slime, metal king slime...) roam, only they appear. Areas without metal monsters stay as they are. The game reads its encounter tables once when it starts, so this takes effect the next time the game starts (the window offers to restart it). In a session with friends everybody has to start with the same choice.

column1: Vanish: walk through monsters until you vanish again
column2: Switch it on, then press L + R + SELECT together in the game to vanish: monsters can no longer start a battle by touching you, so you walk straight through them. Press L + R + SELECT again to show up again. Switching the cheat off also ends the vanishing.
Monsters never run away from a battle: the 'flee' action is refused for them every time, so they pick another one. Metal slimes and other runners stay and fight.
Roaming monsters never notice you, so they don't run after you. A battle still starts if you walk into one.

column1: Walk through monsters (no battles from touching them)
column2: Monsters on the field no longer start a battle when they touch you, so you can walk through them. Story battles still happen.

column1: Quick Save Never Return To Title
column2: After a quick save the game goes on where you were instead of going back to the title screen.
Every vocation shows up in the vocation list of the Vocation Guild, so you can pick any of them. It only changes what the menu offers; your save does not mark them as unlocked (v2 does that).

column1: Every alchemy recipe in the Alchemenu (not yet made)
column2: Every alchemy recipe shows up in the alchemy menu as known but not yet made, so you can cook it.
Press Do it now and the in-game clock jumps to daytime (the sky and the monsters that roam change with it).
Press Do it now and the in-game clock jumps to night (the sky and the monsters that roam change with it).
Your own inn jumps to its top level with every upgrade built.

column1: Whole party: 500 skill points to spend
column2: Sets the unspent skill points of all four party members to 500.

column1: Whole party's HP never goes down
column2: Everyone's HP is refilled to the maximum every frame, so damage never sticks.

column1: Whole party's MP never goes down
column2: Everyone's MP is refilled to the maximum every frame, so casting costs nothing.

column1: HP never goes down in battle
column2: In battle the party's HP stays at the maximum (the European code list's 'Unlimited Health During Battle'). Save before you try it.

column1: MP never goes down in battle
column2: In battle the party's MP stays at the maximum (the European code list's 'Unlimited MP During Battle'). Save before you try it.

column1: Turn the camera all the way round (field and towns)
column2: The camera can be turned all the way round on the field and in towns, not only a little to each side.
The whole game runs as fast as your PC allows, from the moment it starts (Tab does the same while you play). There is no sound while it is fast. Takes effect the next time the game starts.

Skips the waiting time of the DS cartridge when the game loads data. Only while you play alone: in a session with friends the game keeps the real delays so everyone stays in sync. Takes effect the next time the game starts.

Pick a monster from the list: every monster that roams the field (and every companion that joins it) is then that monster, in every area. Story bosses are not affected. The game reads its encounter tables once when it starts, so this takes effect the next time the game starts (the window offers to restart it). In a session with friends everybody has to start with the same choice.

column1: Alchemiracle (great success in the Krak Pot)
column2: Decides the Krak Pot's great success, the Alchemiracle (the pot then makes more or better items than the recipe says). Every time: the chance is set to 100% for each mix, so every mix is an Alchemiracle. Never: the chance is 0%, every mix is a plain success. Alchemy itself never fails in this game. Off: the game's own chance.

column1: Treasure map bosses always drop their chest
column2: The boss at the bottom of a treasure map (grotto) leaves its treasure chest every time you defeat it, so you never have to fight it again for the chest. Which item is inside is still the game's choice.

The plain Attack command of every party member damages all enemies in the battle at once, like a sweeping attack. Damage per enemy is worked out as usual. Switching it off makes attacks single-target again at once.

column1: Unlock All Extra Quests V1, with the Wi-Fi quests
column2: Like V1, but also opens the extra quests that the game used to download over Nintendo Wi-Fi. Use it on a new game before you accept any quest, and do not connect to Wi-Fi afterwards.

column1: Unlock All Extra Quests V2, with the Wi-Fi quests
column2: Like V2, but also opens the extra quests that the game used to download over Nintendo Wi-Fi. Use it after you have finished quests 2, 117 and 120, and do not connect to Wi-Fi afterwards.
